notes.title: It's not just about weapons anymore — defense is strategy too! 🛡️ Patch 4 Notes
notes.content:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/ad3cd65f9b5a3cd40e6f80688c9b2962c658c19a.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Hello everyone,[/p][p][b]Patch 4[/b] for SAVE has been applied.[/p][p]In this update, we’ve introduced a [b]gear slot system[/b] and [b]armor items[/b], focusing on enhancing players’ survival strategies and equipment management.[/p][p][/p][p]Players can now equip various types of armor such as [b]helmets, body armor, and knee pads[/b]. [/p][p]Each piece has its own defense stats and effects, allowing for strategic choices depending on play style and situation.[/p][p]We’ve also added [b]tactical vests and backpacks[/b], which now expand the player's inventory space directly.[/p][p][/p][p]Through this, the overall survival structure has become more layered and in-depth.[/p][p][/p][p]Along with this patch, the inventory UI has been completely revamped.[/p][p]We refined the entire interface to make equipping and removing gear more intuitive and convenient, allowing players to quickly adjust their gear setup based on the situation.[/p][p][/p][p]This patch goes beyond simply adding new items—it is a major turning point that brings more [b]strategy and choice[/b] to SAVE’s combat and survival mechanics.[/p][p]Let’s take a look at what’s changed with Patch 4.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Key Features of Patch 4[/b][/h2][p][/p][h3][b]New Armor and Bag Items[/b][/h3][h3][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/4b65e6b065054f1570798a1d0742d6117c9bb816.png"][/img][/h3][p]In this update, a total of [b]8 armor items[/b] and [b]6 bag items[/b] have been newly added to the [b]Basecamp shop[/b].[/p][p][b]Helmets[/b] come in two types: a lightweight version that provides basic defense, and a heavier version with greater protection.
Each of these two types also has a variant with a built-in [b]tactical light[/b], totaling [b]four types[/b] in all.
They are designed to be useful in both dark areas and combat situations.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Body armor[/b] and [b]knee pads[/b] have two variants each, offering enhanced defense and a wider range of strategic options during survival situations.[/p][p]Players can now purchase and equip all eight types of armor from the shop, adapting their gear to suit different scenarios.[/p][p][/p][p]In addition, [b]3 types of tactical vests[/b] and [b]3 types of backpacks[/b] have been added, allowing for [b]inventory expansion[/b].
These items provide different storage capacities depending on their grade — the more expensive the item, the more slots it offers.[/p][p]As a result, players can now make more efficient equipment choices and resource management decisions based on their strategy and available funds.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Armor Slots and Defense System Added[/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/594964fdcbe348085123615ff5d3897b2bf78606.png"][/img][/p][p]Dedicated gear slots for [b]helmet, body armor, and knee pads[/b] have been added to the inventory UI.[/p][p]Each slot accepts only the matching type of gear, and equipping items increases the player’s [b]defense stat[/b].
The higher the defense, the more incoming damage is reduced, making gear choices a key factor in survival.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Bag Slots and Inventory Expansion[/b][/h3][p]New slots have also been added for [b]tactical vests[/b] and [b]backpacks[/b].[/p][p]Equipping these expands your [b]available inventory slots[/b], allowing you to carry more items and manage your resources more strategically.[/p][p]This system breaks past the old inventory space limitation and opens up various new options in looting routes and mission planning based on your equipment choices.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h2][b]🚢 The Road to Full Release[/b][/h2][p]With Patch 4, SAVE takes another step forward, strengthening its survival mechanics through an equipment-based strategy system.[/p][p][/p][p]Our team has long considered how SAVE can go beyond simply delivering fear, and instead offer a truly immersive experience of [b]exploration, decision-making, cooperation, and conflict[/b].[/p][p]We will continue refining the direction of the game based on these goals.[/p][p][/p][p]We’re still finalizing the timeline and details of the next update, so we can’t share specifics just yet.
However, SAVE’s content and systems are steadily being expanded and polished on the journey toward full release.[/p][p][b]Once the roadmap becomes clearer, we’ll share it first through our official channels.[/b][/p][p][/p][p]SAVE is a game built together with your feedback.[/p][p]If you have suggestions or thoughts while playing, feel free to share them through our [url="https://discord.com/invite/BNPNyEa99F"]official Discord channel.[/url][/p][p]Your voice is always a great support to us.[/p][p]Thank you.[/p]

notes.title: Cooperation or Competition? The Choice is Yours! ⚖️ Patch 3 Notes
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/49385831e945124219065fb3be62a2e3c6c34b96.jpg[/img]
Hello everyone,

We're excited to announce that the third major update for SAVE, Patch 3, has officially been released!

This update focuses on enhancing both cooperation and competition between players. 

Now, players must not only work together to survive and complete missions but also navigate a subtle competitive dynamic, creating a more tense and engaging gameplay experience.


One of the key new features is the introduction of the Team Funds Dashboard, which allows players to clearly see each team member’s individual contributions. 

This enables a form of indirect competition based on performance, all while encouraging team effort.


Additionally, we’ve introduced a new PvP damage system, allowing players to inflict harm on one another. 

Whether by accident or intention, this adds another layer of tension to every operation, making communication and careful decision-making more critical than ever.

To prevent this tension from becoming a source of frustration, we’ve also reworked the revival system. 

Now, you can revive yourself by spending funds, or return to the mission for free with help from a teammate at the base camp—highlighting the value of teamwork even further.


We’ve also made it easier to identify and communicate with teammates by giving each character a distinct appearance, improving both recognition and immersion during cooperative play.

Alongside these changes, we’ve implemented a variety of improvements aimed at enhancing the overall experience and user convenience.

Let’s take a closer look at what’s new in Patch 3!


[h2][b]Key Features of Patch 3[/b][/h2]

[h3][b]Team Fund Status Board[/b][/h3]
We’ve added a Team Fund Status Board UI that lets you check each player’s contribution by interacting with the shop terminal. 

You can now view each player's total spending and sales profit, encouraging indirect competition through visible contribution metrics.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/5c763f046843d41cc7af1610be7d48fc075a42be.png[/img]

[h3][b]Player-vs-Player (PvP) Enabled[/b][/h3]
To increase tension and strategic choice in cooperative operations, players can now inflict damage on each other—intentionally or by accident. 

This adds a new layer of risk, betrayal, and emergent scenarios during missions.

[h3][b]Revival System Improvements[/b][/h3]
To minimize frustration from long downtimes after death, you can now revive yourself using funds after a short wait. 

Alternatively, a teammate who returns to Base Camp can now revive you for free, reinforcing the importance of teamwork.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/192e08ec345bd2bc49fb8802916fa8337debe670.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/e24c6188c556e98af04357534fecae8d3a00221b.png[/img]

[h3][b]Distinct Character Skins[/b][/h3]
Each character now features a unique appearance to help with quick identification and communication during gameplay. 

This also enhances visual diversity and personal expression.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/3b6af1cabf9540cd361b920d90fdbdf656486b15.png[/img]

[h3][b]5th Floor Cabin Layout Overhaul[/b][/h3]
To improve exploration and keep repeat playthroughs fresh, we’ve completely redesigned the cabins on the 5th floor, each with different themes and layouts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/7ad4bd76a46b726a87111d0808a1de9a7999bde1.png[/img]

[h3][b]New Infirmary in Base Camp[/b][/h3]
We’ve added an Infirmary to Base Camp to allow players to quickly heal between missions, improving quality-of-life and preparation flow.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/d4dc76844b7f61a6acc6a26d3982e101c809588e.png[/img]

For more details on usability improvements, bug fixes, and other updates, please check out the full patch notes below!

[h2][b]Patch3 Notes📋[/b][/h2]

[h3][b]Base Camp Updates[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Added a Team Fund Status Board at the shop.
[*]Infirmary has been added.
[*]“Rest” interaction moved inside the Infirmary.
[*]Player status UI now visible in Base Camp.
[*]Returning teammates can now revive fallen players for free.
[*]Voice volume control added to the revive interaction UI.
[/list]

[h3][b]Ship Layout Changes[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Complete redesign of all 5th floor cabins.
[*]Updated interior design of the 5th floor Hospital.
[*]Fixed all sight-blocking issues inside the ship.
[/list]

[h3][b]Item Sales & Shop Adjustments[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Stun Recovery Syringe has been removed from the shop.
[*]All consumable items can now be sold.
[/list]

[h3][b]Usability Improvements[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Players can now self-revive after a cooldown and cost.
[*]UI will now close if a player is attacked while it's open.
[*]Spectator mode now allows switching to dead players.
[/list]

[h3][b]Sound Improvements[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Reduced voice delay when using walkie-talkies.
[*]Tweaked environmental sound ranges and volume inside and outside the ship.
[*]Adjusted sound effects for the lifeboat.
[*]Balanced monster-related SFX volumes.
[/list]

[h3][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Fixed an issue preventing rejoining after leaving a private room.
[/list]


[h2][b]What’s Coming Next[/b][/h2]

In the next update, we're planning to introduce new monsters, along with equippable gear such as armor and bags, allowing for more strategic loadout choices.

We're also prioritizing:
[list]
[*]Enhancing the Sanity system.
[*]Expanding abnormal phenomena aboard the ship.
[/list]

Our goal is to heighten the psychological tension and provide new environmental threats that deepen the horror and unpredictability of exploration.

Thank you all for your ongoing support and valuable feedback. 

SAVE is evolving with every patch, and your ideas help shape its future.

Got thoughts or suggestions? 

Join the conversation on [url=https://discord.com/invite/BNPNyEa99F] our Discord [/url]—we’d love to hear from you!

Thank you!

notes.title: You can now return to the base camp anytime! 🚤 Patch 2 Notes
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/d12c3465e926c8e0d8159b27757a7e7001bcf326.jpg[/img]
Hello, everyone!

It’s already been a month since SAVE launched in Early Access.

As we previously announced, [b]Patch 2 focuses on a major overhaul of the Base Camp system.[/b]

Previously, gameplay followed a fixed loop: Mission Prep → Ship Exploration → Mission Completion.

[b]Now, players can freely travel between the Base Camp and the exploration zones (ships) at any time. [/b]

This major structural change offers greater freedom and strategic flexibility, especially for cooperative play.

You can now return to Base Camp mid-exploration to:

- Sell acquired items
- Upgrade gear
- Purchase consumables

Mission completion is now handled at Base Camp, encouraging more coordinated and tactical team-based strategies.


We’ve also made significant level design improvements inside the ships.

- Missions 1 and 2 have been restructured into a seamless, continuous expedition, making exploration more fluid and immersive.
- Difficulty has been rebalanced to focus more on exploration.
- New areas have been added, expanding the depth and complexity of each run.


With this second major update, SAVE has evolved into a more strategic and dynamic co-op experience—offering fresh gameplay unlike anything before.

Ready to dive in? 

Let’s take a closer look at what’s changed in Patch 2!


[b][h2]Key Features of Patch 2[/h2][/b]
[b][h3]Two-Way Boat Travel Added[/h3][/b]
Previously, traveling between the Base Camp and the ship meant the mission was over, so players couldn’t freely use the Base Camp during a mission.

[b]With this update, you can now return to Base Camp at any time during a mission using the boat.[/b]

We’ve also improved the transport system so that items dropped on the ground will be carried along when traveling by boat or lifeboat. 

This enables more strategic gameplay, such as sending or retrieving items in advance.

As a result, tactical choices based on resource management and role distribution among teammates have expanded significantly.

The boat remains a shared resource among all team members, reinforcing the importance of cooperation and coordination.

And now that you can freely re-enter the ship from Base Camp, we've added a new feature that lets you remotely call the boat back to Base Camp, improving convenience in boat operations.

In previous versions, if a teammate died during a mission, they couldn’t be revived—making further progression much harder.

[b]Now, you can return to Base Camp at any time and revive fallen teammates by spending a certain amount of currency at the Situation Room.[/b]

Even if your team doesn’t have enough money on hand, revives are still possible—with the remaining amount recorded as negative balance. 

This new system ensures the flow of the game continues smoothly, allowing missions to carry on without unnecessary interruptions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/ca166903b87412113e959c7c61215375a61255c2.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/5d3f18b4c6468d2562cd09146382fdf3cb15e028.jpg[/img]

[b][h3]Buy & Sell Items at Base Camp[/h3][/b]
Previously, you could only buy items with funds you had before starting a mission, and earnings from completed missions were pooled to prepare for the next one.

[b]Now, you can return to Base Camp mid-mission to sell items and immediately use the profits to purchase new gear.[/b]

This update gives players greater control over inventory and resources, allowing you to offload unnecessary items and gear up based on current mission needs.

Whether it’s combat, exploration, or survival, you’ll now have more freedom and flexibility to adapt your strategy in real time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/de9ea804a54aa6502a66e2a468dfb5f99a8b1b58.jpg[/img]

[b][h3]Mission Completion System Overhauled[/h3][/b]
Previously, missions could only be completed by collecting all objective items and then escaping together. 

If the team failed to secure all the items—or if someone escaped early while holding key items—the mission would often become stuck or forced to end.

[b]With this update, players can now return to Base Camp and submit collected objective items individually. [/b]

Once all required items have been submitted, the mission will automatically complete, seamlessly transitioning into the next one.

At any point during a mission, anyone can return to Base Camp and interact with the submission box in the Briefing Room to turn in their objective items.

This system greatly improves flexibility in how teams share and manage mission goals, leading to a much more strategic and natural cooperative experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/5d9ca68e50570b5d33ae9d8481ff63016c290363.jpg[/img]

[b][h3]Level Design Rework[/h3][/b]
With the overhaul of the Base Camp system, both the interior and exterior of the ship have been redesigned as persistent exploration zones, no longer tied strictly to mission progression.

This change allows players to actively explore the game world at their own pace, creating opportunities for new discoveries and challenges at any time.

However, to prevent players from feeling lost or overwhelmed in the early stages, we’ve implemented a gradual area expansion system.

Exploration zones now unlock progressively based on mission progress, and certain areas become accessible only after solving specific puzzles.

This new structure ensures a more engaging and rewarding sense of exploration, giving players a steady flow of fresh environments and objectives to uncover.

[b][h3]Difficulty & Balance Adjustments[/h3][/b]
Mission difficulty has been rebalanced to make basic completion relatively accessible, while greater rewards now require taking on more risk and challenge.

This allows players to enjoy the satisfaction of completing core objectives, while also offering strategic depth for those seeking extra profit through bolder decisions.

Rather than simply surviving or finishing missions, the new balance encourages diverse playstyles and approaches, reinforcing the game's overall strategic and risk-reward dynamics.

Difficulty is now more flexible across the board, helping players experience stronger immersion and a greater sense of accomplishment as they adapt their strategies in real time.


For more details on usability improvements, bug fixes, and other changes, please check out the full patch notes below!


[b][h2]Patch2 Notes📋[/h2][/b]
[b]Base Camp Overhaul[/b]
[list]
[*]Boat Position Adjusted: The boat's location within Base Camp has been changed.
[*]Navigation Guide Added: A guideline now directs players to the boat's new position.
[*]Spawn Point Updates: Player spawn locations upon returning to or re-entering Base Camp have been modified.
[*]Situation Room Introduced: A new Situation Room has been added to Base Camp, offering additional functionalities.
[/list]
[b]Boat Operation System Enhancements[/b]
[list]
[*]Mid-Mission Return: Interacting with the boat on the ship no longer ends the mission; players can now return to Base Camp at any time.
[*]Remote Recall: Boats docked at the ship can be remotely summoned back to Base Camp.
[*]Item and Player Transport: Using the boat transports both players and any items inside.
[*]Fuel Requirement: Operating the boat from Base Camp now requires a fuel canister, purchasable from the shop. The first deployment is exempt from this requirement.
[*]Negative Balance Purchases: Fuel canisters can be bought even if team funds are insufficient, resulting in a negative team balance.
[*]Artifact Restriction: Players cannot board the boat while carrying the Mission 2 objective item, the Artifact.
[/list]
[b]Mission Briefing Room Updates[/b]
[list]
[*]Structural Redesign: The interior layout of the Mission Briefing Room has been revamped.
[*]Objective Submission: Interactive objects have been added for players to submit mission objective items.
[/list]
[b]Shop Enhancements[/b]
[list]
[*]Item Transactions: Players can now freely sell and purchase items at Base Camp.
[*]Mission Completion: Submitting objective items now completes missions.
[*]Fuel Availability: Boat fuel canisters are available for purchase.
[*]Early Access Items: Sanity Recovery Pills and Stun Recovery Syringes are now purchasable from the start of the game.
[*]Player Redeployment: Deceased players can be redeployed mid-mission via the Situation Room.
[/list]
[b]Situation Room Features[/b]
[list]
[*]Revival Mechanic: Players can revive fallen teammates using the "Redeploy" function.
[*]Negative Balance Revivals: Revival is possible even with insufficient team funds, leading to a negative balance.
[*]Radio Interaction Relocation: The "Turn Off Radio" interaction has been repositioned within the Situation Room.
[*]Boat Recall Interaction: A new interaction to recall the boat has been added to the Situation Room.​
[/list]
[b]Lifeboat System Adjustments[/b]
[list]
[*]Transport Functionality: Activating the lifeboat with all necessary items transports both players and items to Base Camp.
[*]One-Way Travel: Returning to the ship from Base Camp via lifeboat is no longer possible.
[*]Dual Lifeboat Access: Both lifeboats on the ship are now operational.
[/list]
[b]Ship Level Design Modifications[/b]
[list]
[*]New Engine Room: An Engine Room has been added to the ship's interior.
[*]Door Lock Changes: Some doors now have different locking mechanisms, altering accessible areas.
[*]Password-Protected Areas: New sections accessible only via password entry have been introduced.
[*]Anomaly Adjustments: Conditions and locations for anomalies like walls and flames have been modified.
[*]Monster Spawn Tweaks: 
- Beast-Type Monsters: Spawn conditions have been altered.
- Humanoid Monsters: Spawn locations and conditions have been adjusted.
[*]Item Spawn Changes:
- Mission 1 Objectives: Spawn locations have been updated.
- Lifeboat Parts: Quantities and locations have been modified.
- Consumables: Quantities on the ship have been adjusted.
- Sellable Items: Quantities on the ship have been adjusted.
- Destructible Objects: Quantities on the ship have been adjusted.
[/list]
[b]Balance Adjustments[/b]
[list]
[*]Starting Funds: Initial team funds set to $3,500.
[*]Additional Player Funds: Each additional player contributes $1,000 to team funds.
[*]Item Price Changes:
- Tactical Knife: $350 → $500
- Tactical Light: $150 → $300
- Radio: $150 → $200
- 9mm Pistol: $1,100 → $2,000
[*]Monster Behavior:
- Attack Delay: Increased between consecutive attacks.
- Stun Duration: Extended from 30 seconds to 2 minutes.
[*]Revival Cost: Player redeployment cost reduced from $4,000 to $2,000.
[/list]
[b]Usability Improvements[/b]
[list]
[*]Control Settings: A key usage list has been added to the Control tab in the settings menu.
[*]Door Unlock Persistence: Card key and digital number lock doors now remain unlocked after initial access.
[/list]
[b]Visual and Cinematic Updates[/b]
[list]
[*]Transition Sequences: Animations between Base Camp and ship travel have been completely overhauled.
[*]Mission Start and Success: New animations have been introduced.
[*]Ending Sequence: The final mission's ending animation has been enhanced.
[/list]
[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*]Spectator Mode Issue: Resolved an intermittent issue where the screen would freeze instead of transitioning to spectator mode upon death.
[*]Item Interaction Bug: Fixed a problem where items near the boat on the ship couldn't be interacted with.
[*]Radio Notification: Addressed an issue where radio alerts would occasionally not play.
[/list]
[b]Known Issues Addressed[/b]
[list]
[*]Private Room Reconnection: Fixed the inability to reconnect after entering a private room.
[*]Post-Mission Failure Glitch: Resolved an issue where game objects would appear in the lobby after mission failure.
[*]Performance on Low-End Hosts: Addressed a problem where the game would freeze or crash when numerous monsters spawned on hosts with below-recommended PC specifications.
[/list]


[b][h2]Upcoming Update – Patch 3 Preview[/h2][/b]
[b]In the upcoming Patch 3, we’re focusing on enhancing the fun of playing together with expanded community-based features.[/b]

You can look forward to new systems that not only strengthen cooperation among teammates but also occasionally introduce elements of competition—broadening the scope and excitement of team-based gameplay.

We're also preparing a significant content expansion, including the addition of Mission 3 and deeper exploration elements within the ship.

notes.title: Automatic door closing has been removed! 💣 SAVE Patch1 Note
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/4179875ae408b8b3045fe063c3def6961e897fd6.png[/img]

Hello everyone!

It's already been a week since SAVE launched in Early Access!

First and foremost, we sincerely thank everyone who has purchased and played the Early Access version.

Over the past week, we've been gathering and analyzing your feedback to refine the direction of SAVE and improve the overall experience. 

We're committed to enhancing the game and have been working on an update to address key issue.



[h3][b]Early Access Patch 1 Overview[/b][/h3]

This update focuses on removing elements that disrupt immersion and making the gameplay flow more natural.

Doors that previously closed automatically will now remain open.

Interaction indicators and item collection prompts have been improved to provide clearer guidance for exploration.

Mission 1 has been adjusted to reduce excessive exploration time, making key objectives more accessible and reducing fatigue from repetition.

Level design, balance adjustments, sound and UI improvements, and bug fixes have been implemented to enhance usability and the overall player experience.

We have prepared the first patch reflecting these changes. 

Full details are provided in the Patch Notes below.



[h3][b]Patch 1 Note📋[/b][/h3]

[b]Usability Improvements[/b]
[list]
[*]Doors in hallways will no longer automatically close when a player is nearby.
[*]Cabin doors will no longer close automatically.
[*]Added a pop-up notification to prevent mission objective items from being incorrectly registered due to server lag in multiplayer.
[*]Interaction UI will now highlight objects even if they are slightly out of range, as long as they are visible.
[*]Added key control instructions at Base Camp.
[*]Adjusted FOV for spectator camera.
[/list]
[b]Level Design Adjustments[/b]
[list]
[*]Stairway doors are now painted yellow and feature additional signage for better visibility.
[*]Improved lighting in darker stairwells to enhance visibility.
[*]Added current location markers on floor maps for better navigation.
[*]Removed unused doors for a cleaner level layout.
[/list]
[b]Mission 2 Level Design Changes[/b]
[list]
[*]Removed the ability to collect all lifeboat parts in one location on the third floor.
[*]Adjusted spawn locations for some lifeboat parts.
[*]Modified roaming paths for artifacts.
[*]Adjusted spawn points for humanoid monsters.
[*]Changed the spawn conditions for beast-type monsters.
[/list]
[b]Mission 1 Level Design Changes[/b]
[list]
[*]Doors that previously required a keycard to open are now unlocked by default.
[*]Adjusted spawn locations for key objectives to be more intuitive.
[*]Only specific humanoid monsters will now drop cabin keys.
[*]Some previously locked cabin doors are now open by default.
[*]Adjusted Doppelgänger spawn conditions.
[*]Changed some humanoid monster spawn locations.
[*]Drastically shortened the maze section in the latter part of the mission to reduce exploration fatigue.
[/list]
[b]Balance Adjustments[/b]
[list]
[*]Healing syringe effectiveness reduced from 80 → 40.
[*]Stamina required to sprint reduced from 50% → 40%.
[*]Stamina recovery delay reduced from 3s → 1s.
[*]Stamina drain while sprinting reduced from 8/sec → 7/sec.
[*]Inventory size of the tablet relic reduced from 3×3 → 2×2.
[/list]
[b]Additional Features[/b]
[list]
[*]Improved voice chat volume for better communication.
[*]Increased maximum sound volume settings in the options menu.
[/list]
[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*]Fixed an issue where some radios could not be destroyed by monsters.
[*]Fixed an issue where some radios overlapped destructible objects.
[*]Fixed a bug where players who died in specific locations could not retrieve dropped items.
[*]Removed an unnecessary animation that played when attacking with an empty slot.
[*]Added collision boxes to prevent falling deaths near lifeboat boarding areas.
[/list]


[h3][b]Future Update Plans[/b][/h3]

Many of you have shared valuable feedback about SAVE, particularly regarding the inconvenience of having to restart from Mission 1 if you fail to complete Mission 2 after a difficult challenge.

From the early stages of SAVE’s design, we structured the game so that small choices in Mission 1—such as unlocking doors or leaving items behind—would organically impact Mission 2.

Through these elements, we aimed to create a game where each playthrough would offer a different experience depending on each team member’s decisions and playstyle.

Additionally, we wanted SAVE to be a challenging game that fosters a strong sense of accomplishment as players cooperate from the beginning to overcome obstacles.

[b]For this reason, we initially believed that starting from specific points with the same progress or joining mid-mission without participating from the beginning could negatively impact the intended SAVE experience.[/b]


However, your feedback has made us realize that, rather than fostering the joy of improvement through repeated challenges, SAVE’s current difficulty structure often leads to frustration due to its long and complex mission paths.

In particular, we found that some players feel overwhelmed by the need to repeat Mission 1.

With this in mind, we plan to refine SAVE in the following ways:
 [code][b]Making mission completion simpler and more straightforward

Making the preparation process for the next mission more challenging

Providing more freedom and strategic choices within missions[/b] [/code]
In future updates, we will introduce a system allowing players to return to the basecamp anytime to buy and sell items, expand the range of ship exploration, and enhance the vessel’s interior with more challenging elements.

Through these changes, we aim to create a structure where players can collaborate freely with their teammates and clear missions in a variety of ways.


We will continue refining SAVE before its full release, ensuring that players can find new strategies and enjoyment even in repeated playthroughs.

We are committed to delivering a more polished game through future updates, and we always welcome your feedback! 😊

Please feel free to share your experiences, suggestions, and ideas on our[url=
https://discord.com/invite/BNPNyEa99F] Discord Channel[/url].

Thank you for playing SAVE! 🚢

notes.title: Dev Log #6: Co-op & Cosmic phenomena
notes.content:
[h4]Hello, Everyone![/h4]

In this devlog, we’re excited to introduce the latest updates on the co-op mode and cosmic phenomena that many of you have been eagerly anticipating.

If you want to receive the latest updates on SAVE as quickly as possible, be sure to join our Discord community! We’ll be sharing regular updates there, so don’t forget to follow and wishlist the game as well!

Now, let’s take a look at the newly added content! 

[h3]Co-op mode🙌[/h3]

SAVE’s real-time co-op mode supports 1–4 players, allowing you to communicate and strategically carry out operations with your team. We’ve dedicated a lot of time and effort to ensuring that you and your teammates can work together to overcome the cosmic phenomena and threats aboard the SENARA. 

As part of this update, we’ve added a voice chat system and a Base Camp where players can prepare for missions and plan their strategies. These features will enhance teamwork, immerse you in cooperative gameplay, and help you tackle challenging missions together. 

 [previewyoutube=UMXjl4HSelI;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Voice Chat System🔊[/h3]

A crucial element of co-op gameplay, the voice chat system, has now been integrated into SAVE. This system enhances strategic communication, ensuring that players stay immersed from mission preparation to execution.

By enabling voice chat in the settings, players can choose between two communication methods:

[b]● Proximity Voice Chat 📢[/b]
Players must be close to hear each other, creating a realistic and immersive communication experience. 

[b]● Walkie Talkie Voice Chat📡[/b]
Players can purchase a Walkie Talkie from the equipment shop, allowing them to communicate regardless of distance. This ensures that important information can be shared quickly and enables more strategic cooperation.

[h3]Base Camp🚢[/h3] 
Introducing Base Camp, your mission preparation and strategy hub!

At Base Camp, you can access key facilities such as the Operation Board, Equipment Shop, and Rubber Boat, all of which are crucial for planning and executing missions. This space also serves as an important part of USTC’s lore and narrative, enhancing your immersion in the world of SAVE.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/67c6ce68404b09b647a09fbfc8c023274d87e301.png[/img]
[h3]Equipment Shop🛒[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/dad061e76254915f88162227657a5098ff5d6608.png[/img]
Purchase weapons, armor, and other gear provided by Miskatonic University to ensure a well-prepared strategy.

[h3]Operations Board📋 [/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/7c1913ebf608e1538cc677382c5371e58028c8cf.png[/img]
The room has displays that show the mission progress and objectives, helping teams plan their approach effectively.

[h3]Rubber Boat🚤[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/b0a4fdc35369aeca2c6ef28b620e7875c4d4d7de.png[/img]
A staging area for final preparations before deployment, allowing players to gear up before infiltrating the ship.
[h3]Cosmic Phenomena  [/h3]

Cosmic phenomena are a core element of Lovecraftian horror, bringing eerie, unexplainable occurrences and existential threats to the SENARA. These events create an immersive and tense atmosphere, keeping players on edge throughout their journey.

Throughout the ship, mysterious cosmic disturbances will occur, and encountering them can lead to sanity loss, health depletion, and other dangers. Each phenomenon has its own unique patterns and countermeasures, requiring players to analyze and respond strategically.

These eerie encounters will keep you in a constant state of tension, making your exploration even more intense.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/rh2madM.gif[/img] 

In this devlog, we introduced cosmic phenomena and the long-awaited co-op mode. We’ll continue to share more content and development updates in the future, so stay tuned for the next devlog!

If you have any questions or feedback, feel free to reach out via our Discord channel. Your valuable input is always a great source of motivation for us.

Thank you! 😊

notes.title: Dev Log #5: New Level & Sanity System

If you want to be the first to receive the latest updates on SAVE, make sure to join our Discord community! We’ll be sharing updates regularly, so don’t forget to follow and wishlist the game as well!

Now, let’s take a look at the newly added content! 

[h3]🚢 New Levels on the SENARA[/h3]

The newly added levels are designed to let you explore the background and hidden stories of the SENARA. As you navigate through these environments, you will uncover the ship’s true nature and immerse yourself in its eerie narrative.

These spaces serve as a medium to convey the narrative elements of SAVE, allowing you to slowly unravel the secrets of the SENARA through exploration. Now, let’s introduce the new levels.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/f60e83f02f28522842e787bbd6430cf45069513d.png[/img]

notes.content:
Hello, everyone

We hope you all had a wonderful holiday season!

Our team has been hard at work, and just like last year, we're kicking off this year with a renewed commitment to making SAVE an even more polished and exciting game for you all.

Your valuable feedback from last year’s alpha playtest has been a major inspiration for our development team.

In this dev blog, we’re excited to share updates on the newly updated levels and the Graphic settings feature we’ve been working on.

Now, let’s dive into what’s new and improved since the alpha playtest, shall we?

[h3]1. Updated Levels 🚢[/h3]

During the alpha playtest, we aimed to create a serene yet eerie atmosphere by setting the game in the misty morning hours, with a calm and silent ocean as the backdrop.

However, to enhance the narrative flow and intensify the tension, we’ve shifted the game’s timeline to 2 a.m. midnight, adjusting the background levels to emphasize the dark atmosphere of the night sea.

With this change, we hope you’ll experience an even greater sense of psychological horror as you explore the SENARA. Experiencing the deep darkness and eerie silences of the night sea and feel the tension as you navigate.

[previewyoutube=EH0gjNhiUws;full][/previewyoutube]

During the alpha playtest, we received feedback regarding the lack of customizable graphics options, which caused inconvenience for many of you. To fix this, improving the graphics options was one of the first things we focused on after the playtest ended.

As a result, we’ve not only introduced a variety of new graphics settings but also achieved significant optimization in rendering performance along the way. Players can now adjust the rendering scale, toggle ray tracing, and utilize advanced features such as DLSS for upscaled rendering.

These enhancements allow for flexible graphics settings adjustable to the player's hardware and preference. Moreover ensuring a smoother and more visually immersive experience in SAVE.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/jMgNbIn.gif[/img]

We hope you like what we have prepared in the devlog, where we shared updates on the new graphics settings and level updates.

Before we begin, we’d like to thank everyone for their incredible support and participation in the Alpha Test. We hope that you guys had a blast playing SAVE!

We sadly have to inform you that on December 20th, we will be closing the playtest!

When there is bad news, there is good news! The good news is that we will be back with a DEMO of SAVE in February 2025 with new content, more, and improved gameplay! Moreover, we have all heard your feedback regarding narrative, co-op, monsters, etc. We greatly appreciate your feedback and suggestions and will reflect on your feedback. Moreover, we will develop and incorporate it as the key to making SAVE.

Moreover, shall we review our responses to your feedback and examine the new content in the demo?

[h2]Frequently Asked Question🤔[/h2]

[h5]Q: In the future, will there be some narrative to the game?[/h5] 

I felt that the connection between the teaser and the alpha test was lacking in the story. The religious yet terrifying atmosphere was particularly captivating in the teaser. Still, in the main game, there was not much of a narrative we had expected.

[quote] A: Thank you for showing interest in our story and atmosphere. We’re planning to deliver the narrative in various ways, going beyond simple text-based storytelling. Additionally, the horror atmosphere will be further enhanced as key features are gradually implemented. The religious and psychological horror experiences showcased in the teaser will also be a core part of the full game’s content.
[/quote]
[h5]Q: Will more horror elements be added in the future?[/h5]

The teaser showcased a highly realistic and religious atmosphere, creating a unique element of horror. However, in the current version, while tense situations like being chased by monsters have been added, it feels like the horror elements from the teaser have been reduced.

[quote] A: We fully understand and agree with the points you’ve raised, and we are working on improvements to address them. As the planned elements are introduced, the ship will transform into an even more grotesque and horrifying environment. Additionally, areas related to the religious atmosphere will be revealed soon, so you can look forward to more intense and immersive horror elements in the future.
[/quote]
[h5]Q: When will the co-op feature be supported?[/h5]

The gameplay goal of collecting money seems fun, but it feels like co-op play would make the experience significantly better.

[quote] A: Cooperative gameplay is one of the core directions of our game. In the upcoming demo version, we’ve prepared multiplayer content tailored for a 4-player experience. Moving forward, we’ll introduce a variety of elements to further enhance the fun and engagement of cooperative play.
[/quote]
[h5]Q: What direction will the gameplay take in the future?[/h5]

In the alpha test, I experienced two gameplay styles: finding and using lifeboat-related items to escape and collecting items to reach a target goal. Each had its pros and cons. What direction will the gameplay take in the future?

[quote] A: We are currently designing the gameplay around multiple mission types, combining elements from the alpha version and the teaser. In the full release, you’ll be able to fully experience these diverse escape mechanics and missions as complete content. Stay tuned for what’s to come!
[/quote]
[h5]Q: Will there be single-player content for single players?[/h5]

If the game emphasizes co-op play, many players who enjoyed the single-player experience from the teaser might feel left out. Will there be a separate single-player mode?

[quote]A: While we are focusing on developing cooperative gameplay, we are also implementing safeguards to ensure an equally immersive single-player experience. In single-player mode, you’ll face even more isolated and challenging situations. However, we’ve prepared special rewards that make it worth the challenge, so we encourage you to take it on solo as well!
[/quote]
[h5]Q: Will there be new monsters and improvements of the monsters in the future? [/h5]

The initial appearance of the monsters was great, but their movements and behavior afterward felt somewhat lacking. Can we expect new monsters to be added?

[quote]A: Through testing, we have identified issues with the monster AI and movement, and we are actively working on improvements. In future updates, you can expect more refined AI, immersive movements, and additional monsters designed to maximize tension and elevate the horror experience.
[/quote]
[h2] What to expect in the future?🚀[/h2]

As the technical test is over, we will be going on developing more features and enhancing the gameplay. Here are some upcoming features you guys can expect in the future:

[*]New Varieties of Mission
[*]Coop System & Voice Chat System
[*]Cosmic Phenomenon
[*]Narrative
[*]And More…..

We hope you guys like what we have prepared! Moreover, we will be posting dev logs about our WIP (Work in Progress) and our new features as we make progress in our development! So, be sure to follow and wishlist SAVE for upcoming news!

We thank all the players who participated in the alpha test. This period has been filled with excitement for the community and our team. Still, it has also presented us with numerous challenges we seek to solve. We always appreciate and welcome your feedback, and we will continue to listen and respond to you by making SAVE more enjoyable to play.

Moreover, be sure to stay tuned for more announcements about SAVE. If you have any questions or feedback, feel free to share them in the comments below or on [url=https://discord.com/invite/BNPNyEa99F]Discord[/url].

Thank you

notes.title: Alpha Test Gameplay Update
notes.content:
Hello, Agents!

First, we would like to extend our heartfelt gratitude to all agents who applied and actively participated in the alpha test! 🙏

This update has been prepared to enhance the fun of gameplay and incorporate your invaluable feedback. While the previous test primarily focused on functional elements, this time, we've concentrated on significantly improving and expanding gameplay-related content.

We will continue to update and refine the test based on your input, so we greatly appreciate your continued excitement and participation! 😊

Now, let's dive into the key updates for this patch!

[h3]Key Update Details[/h3]

[b]1. Gameplay Changes[/b]

[*][b]Mission Objective System Added[/b]

Each stage now has a target quota to achieve, and failing to meet it will result in mission failure. Clearing the target score unlocks the next stage.
※ The quota can be checked in the game lobby and during gameplay.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/ef6fab202154a433891165e9795ec6617025f56c.png[/img]
[*] [b]Item Collection and Escape[/b]

To achieve the target score, collect various items within the time limit and use the PLB to evade threats and escape.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/60a4728117bfaa51f3b65c8c74800ef3d3c86879.png[/img]

[b]2. Security Card System Added[/b]

[*]Security cards are now required to unlock locked containers (key lockers and safes).
[*]Identify the locker’s serial number and input the matching code from the security card to unlock it.

[previewyoutube=ltW33A_DVjA;full][/previewyoutube]
[b]3. Gameplay Adjustments[/b]

[*][b]Door Spawn Update[/b]
Based on feedback, we've improved the locked state of doors and passages. Most corridor, cabin, and storage doors are now open
[*][b]Room Key Update [/b]
Keys now spawn only for rooms on the current floor, reducing unnecessary movement.
[*][b]Safes Added[/b]
Safes have been added to locked rooms. Unlocking them with security cards grants significant rewards
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/671682419cff91fc62212e88142f75c6d86fd541.png[/img]

[b]4. Starting Items Updated[/b]
[*]Players now start with a flashlight, knife,  pistol, ammunition, a PLB, and a security card.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/1c5e7ec947b2d00964c9669dec0d5ad349ec1749.png[/img]
[b]5. Monster Spawn Rules Updated[/b]

[*]New monster spawn mechanics have been introduced to ensure more intense and suspenseful gameplay.

[b]Patch Note Log[/b]

[*]Lifeboat Usage Disabled
 Lifeboats are no longer accessible.
[*]Level Lighting Improved
Enhanced lighting effects for a more immersive environment.
[*]Camera Tilt Issue Fixed
Resolved a problem causing camera distortions.
[*]PLB Escape Sound Issue Fixed
Fixed external noise issues occurring during PLB escapes.

Thank you for taking the time to read through this update! We hope you enjoy the improvements we’ve made. If you have any questions or suggestions, feel free to leave a comment below or share your thoughts on Discord.

Thank you!

notes.title: SAVE Alpha Playtest is Now Live!
notes.content:
[h3]Hello Everyone 👋[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121196/709f2f7b807011ca9dd6eb1b4c6acf7d87af3443.png[/img]

SAVE Alpha Play Test has begun! Thank you everyone for signing up for alpha test. Hope you will like it! 

The Alpha test to assess the game's performance in a live setting, gather feedback, and evaluate the player experience across multiple areas. please note that SAVE is still in development and this alpha play test is not representative of the final state of the game. 

Moreover during the alpha we plan to have an update regarding difficulty & game-play 🙂 

[h3] Director's Message ✉[/h3]
[quote] Hello everyone,

Thank you so much for participating in the SAVE playtest! Your interest and support mean the world to us.

We sincerely appreciate you taking the time to join us, and we apologize for not being able to provide a more polished version. This playtest is important to us because we believe that listening to your feedback early in development and incorporating it is the key to making SAVE the best game it can be.

As we continue to develop SAVE, we are committed to listening to your input and building the game based on your valuable feedback. We will keep you updated on our progress and future plans,. During the playtest, we’ll be making continuous updates according your feedback.

If you believe in the potential of SAVE and share your valuable feedback, we will do our best to make SAVE a game that more people can enjoy.
[i]- SAVE, Director[/i] [/quote]
Now, let’s go over the information about the play test! 

[h3]Alpha Test Schedule 📆[/h3]
November 27th 2024 

[h3]About[/h3]

SAVE is a Survival deep sea horror game sets in the eerie depths of an abandoned 6,000-Ton Ship 'SENARA', where every shadow holds a secret, and every corner could be your last. Unravel the mysteries and safely escape avoiding relentless threats that prowl in the darkness

[h3]Alpha Test Gameplay Description[/h3]

In this test, you'll experience the core gameplay of SAVE in a single-player mode. Your mission is to infiltrate the SENARA, locate the right entrance to the ship’s interior, collect items, and escape. Remember, unknown threats and phenomena await you!

[h3]Alpha Features[/h3]
[list]
[*] A full experience of the core game play
[*] Encounter 2 Monsters, each with distinct behaviors and unique abilities
[*] 2 Escape Routes with unique requirements for escape
[*] Drowning system
[/list]
[h3]Minimum System Requirements 🖥[/h3]
[list]
[*] OS: Windows 10
[*] Processor: Intel Core i7-8700
[*] Memory: 16GB RAM
[*] Graphics: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 2060
[*] DirectX: Version 11
[*] Storage: At least 4GB available space
[/list]
[h3]We Need Your Feedback![/h3]

During the play test, we hope you guys have fun playing SAVE and share your feedback and opinions about the game! There is a feedback form Here! Our long term goal with this game is to work alongside our community to continually improve, iterate and develop with the players feedback and suggestions in mind in order to deliver a game that is enjoyable and accessible for everyone.

Whoa, hope you like what we prepared :) We are as excited as you are to welcome you. If you have any questions or feedback, feel free to leave them in the comments below or on [url=https://discord.com/invite/BNPNyEa99F]Discord.[/url]

Thank You
